episode_title: Are New Hire Probationary Periods Still a Thing? with John Hagan

real_qa.q: What did the Fifth Circuit rule in Brinja v. Corpus Christi hospital regarding probationary period extensions as adverse employment actions?
real_qa.r: The Fifth Circuit accepted the argument that extending a probationary period can be an adverse employment action. The court held that the nurse could have suffered harm by her probation being extended because she would not have gained any seniority during the extension and was subject to termination without cause, whereas other newly hired nurses were not subject to these conditions.
real_qa.requete: Brinja Fifth Circuit probationary period adverse employment action

real_qa.q: How did the United States Supreme Court case Muldrow v. St. Louis expand the definition of adverse employment action in discrimination cases?
real_qa.r: The United States Supreme Court held in Muldrow v. St. Louis that a plaintiff or employee only had to prove some harm, not an ultimate employment action was taken against her. This represented a watershed shift from the prior requirement that adverse actions had to be ultimate employment decisions such as firing, demotion, or failure to promote.
real_qa.requete: Muldrow v. St. Louis Supreme Court adverse employment action harm

real_qa.q: What are the three recommended steps employers should take regarding orientation periods following the Brinja and Muldrow rulings?
real_qa.r: First, call it an orientation period, not a probationary period, because case law says that getting off probation means you cannot be fired except for just cause. Second, make sure the extension of the orientation period does not carry any penalties with it, such as suspended seniority accrual. Third, make your orientation periods 180 days for all new hires into your company to reduce the frequency of having to extend an orientation period and ensure equal treatment, which is the definition of non-discrimination.
real_qa.requete: orientation period probationary period best practices employers 180 days

real_qa.q: What documentation failures in the Brinja hospital's hostile work environment investigation led to the case being sent back to trial?
real_qa.r: The hospital had multiple investigation problems: documents identified by witnesses supporting the extended probation claim were never produced; managers contradicted each other about the reasons for the extended probation; information contradicted the hospital's position that they did not create a hostile work environment; witnesses were not allowed to sign their own statements that the hospital wrote for them; and a black nurse who was a key witness was never interviewed, even though one manager claimed she had been.
real_qa.requete: hostile work environment investigation documentation witness statements employer

real_qa.q: Why do juries and judges award lower damages or dismiss discrimination claims when an employee is fired during their probationary or orientation period?
real_qa.r: Juries and judges are much less likely to award damages to an employee fired during an orientation period regardless of documentation quality or training provided. Judges and arbitrators accept that during an orientation period, you can be fired for any reason or no reason. Additionally, under the same actor doctrine in the Fifth Circuit, if the person who hired the employee is the same person who fired them, a strong legal inference is created that no discrimination took place, since it does not make logical sense to discriminate at firing for the same characteristics known at hiring.
real_qa.requete: probationary period orientation discrimination claims damages jury less likely
